tasks.title: Project Setup and TypeScript Configuration
tasks.description: Initialize the project repository with TypeScript configuration, build system, and required dependencies for MCP server development.
tasks.details:
1. Create a new repository for the Calendar MCP Server
2. Initialize npm project with `npm init -y`
3. Install TypeScript and required dependencies:
   - TypeScript v5.0+ (`npm install typescript --save-dev`)
   - Node.js types (`npm install @types/node --save-dev`)
   - ts-node for development (`npm install ts-node --save-dev`)
   - ESLint for code quality (`npm install eslint @typescript-eslint/parser @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin --save-dev`)
4. Configure TypeScript (tsconfig.json):
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "strict": true,
    "outDir": "./dist",
    "declaration": true,
    "sourceMap": true,
    "rootDir": "./src"
  },
  "include": ["src/**/*"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist"]
}
```
5. Setup build scripts in package.json:
```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc",
    "dev": "ts-node src/index.ts",
    "lint": "eslint . --ext .ts",
    "test": "jest"
  }
}
```
6. Create basic folder structure:
   - src/ (source code)
   - tests/ (test files)
   - dist/ (compiled output)
7. Install MCP dependencies:
   - Model Context Protocol library (`npm install @modelcontextprotocol/core`)
8. Configure Jest for testing:
   - Install Jest (`npm install jest ts-jest @types/jest --save-dev`)
   - Create jest.config.js
9. Create .gitignore file with appropriate entries for Node.js/TypeScript projects

<info added on 2025-09-19T07:39:55.811Z>
Research findings: The @modelcontextprotocol/core package doesn't appear to exist on npm. After examining the reference implementation at https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/tree/main/src/everything, it seems the MCP server implementation uses a different approach.

Instead of using a pre-packaged SDK, we should:
1. Clone the reference repository for guidance
2. Implement the MCP protocol directly based on the reference implementation
3. Focus on the protocol specification rather than looking for a non-existent package
4. Consider implementing the server components from scratch following the protocol documentation
5. Examine how the reference implementation handles request/response formats, authentication, and tool registration

We'll need to revise our implementation approach to build the core MCP server functionality without relying on an external package.
</info added on 2025-09-19T07:39:55.811Z>
<info added on 2025-09-19T07:41:23.373Z>
<info added on 2025-09-20T14:22:10.456Z>
UPDATE: Successfully identified and installed the correct MCP SDK package.

The official MCP TypeScript SDK has been installed:
- Package: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.18.1
- Source: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk
- This is the official TypeScript SDK for implementing Model Context Protocol servers and clients

The SDK provides comprehensive functionality:
- Server implementation classes (McpServer)
- Client implementation classes (Client)
- Transport options (Stdio, HTTP, SSE, StreamableHTTP)
- Tool, resource, and prompt handling capabilities
- Authentication support
- Full TypeScript type definitions

This package replaces our previous approach of implementing from scratch. We can now leverage the official SDK to build our Calendar MCP Server implementation, which will significantly streamline development.
</info added on 2025-09-20T14:22:10.456Z>
